newsitem.title: FRANCE: France urges Israel to stick by Oslo accords.
newsitem.headline: France urges Israel to stick by Oslo accords.

text.p: France urged Israel on Monday to stick to the Oslo peace accords signed with the Palestinians, saying this was the only way of ending violence.

"It is our conviction that the Palestinian question must be rapidly given a fair and lasting solution. That must be achieved through the full implementation of the Oslo accords," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told reporters.

The Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) last week rejected a proposal from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to complete within six months the Israeli-Palestinian "final status" peace talks, nearly two years earlier than planned.
Final status talks will tackle the thorniest issues dividing Israel and the Palestinians, including borders, Jewish settlements, refugees and the status of Jerusalem.
"There must be an end to violence otherwise the peace process as a whole will be in serious danger," Rummelhardt said.
"Only a return to the letter and the spirit of the signed accords and the enactment of all the provisions of the peace process can serve this end," he added.
